$comment: Ground truth for A1's parser-hardening suite (PLAN.md 7.4).
Every file in Fixtures/hostile/ is deliberately malformed test data. None of it
is ever executed. Run this suite under ASan with a 2 s per-case timeout.
expectedError is the SheetError.code the reader MUST produce; alsoAcceptable
lists codes that indicate the same defence firing at a different layer.
One entry (zip-bomb-nested.xlsx) expects SUCCESS - read its notes.
RECONCILED IN WAVE 1 (addendum 6): the codes below were written against a proposed
naming scheme before A0's SheetError enum existed. A0's enum is the source of truth,
so A1 rewrote every expectedError/alsoAcceptable string to a real SheetError.code and
corrected the Limits.* names. SheetFormatTests/Read/HostileFixtureTests asserts both
that every code here is one the enum can emit and that every fixture has an entry.

errorCodeNamespaces.zip.*: MiniZip.Reader rejections - archive structure, entry names, size caps
errorCodeNamespaces.xml.*: hardened XML pull-parser rejections - DTD, entities, depth, characters, encoding
errorCodeNamespaces.workbook.*: SheetFormat rejections about the package as a whole - missing critical part, encryption, declared sheet dimensions
errorCodeNamespaces.ref.* / cell.*: SheetFormat rejections about one address or one cell's contents

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.limit: Limits.maxCompressionRatio (100:1), enforced above a 1 MB output floor
cases.proves: xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml inflates ~1030:1 to 200 MB. The per-entry ratio cap must fire DURING inflation, not after.
cases.notes: Inflate incrementally and abort mid-stream; a reader that inflates to a buffer first has already lost 200 MB of RAM by the time it checks.

cases.proves: A two-level zip bomb parked in xl/media/. The workbook is otherwise valid, so the CORRECT behaviour is to open it and never inflate that entry - OpaqueParts keeps the compressed bytes.
cases.notes: This is the 'do not be eager' test. PLAN.md 5.2 says keep raw entries; A1's brief says 'do not decompress entries nobody asked for'. This file proves it.

mustNotHappen: the string 'root:' appearing in any cell value
cases.proves: sharedStrings declares external entities pointing at /etc/passwd and at a localhost URL. Neither may be resolved.
cases.notes: XMLParser: shouldResolveExternalEntities = false AND externalEntityResolvingPolicy = .never. Setting only one of them is not enough.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.limit: none - DTDs are refused outright, so no expansion budget is ever needed
cases.proves: Nine levels of 10x entity expansion: &lol9; is 1,000,000,000 characters of 'lol'.
cases.notes: If DTDs are refused outright this never gets a chance to expand, which is the outcome we want - and is why there is no entity-expansion limit in Limits.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: A DOCTYPE with nothing malicious in it. The policy must be blanket - 'no DTDs in OOXML, ever' - not a heuristic that looks for the word SYSTEM.
cases.notes: No legitimate xlsx producer emits a DOCTYPE. Rejecting all of them costs nothing.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: Entry names containing ../ in POSIX and \..\ in Windows form. OpenSheets never extracts to disk, but OpaqueParts is keyed by entry name and A2 writes those names back out - a traversal name must never reach a file API.
cases.notes: Reject on the name, before any inflation, and check the Windows separator too.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: Absolute POSIX and Windows entry names. Python's own zipfile.extract() strips these; a hand-rolled reader that does not is a write-anywhere primitive.
cases.notes: SheetError.archivePathTraversal covers absolute names as well as '..' segments - see its documentation, which names '..', a leading separator, a NUL and a Windows drive letter as one rejection.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: An entry name with an embedded NUL, so a C-string API sees 'xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml' while the zip index sees something else.
cases.notes: Classic poisoned-NUL confusion. Validate names as bytes, not as C strings. SheetError.archivePathTraversal documents NUL, a leading separator and a drive letter as the same rejection, so all three name fixtures share the zip.pathTraversal code.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: Two entries both named xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml with different content. Whichever one a reader picks, some other tool picks the other - so refuse the file.
cases.notes: A1 must reject; A2 must never be able to EMIT a duplicate either.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: The first 55% of a valid xlsx - no end-of-central-directory record at all. This is what a file caught mid-write looks like (PLAN.md 9), so it must be a clean, retryable error rather than a crash.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: A PDF renamed to .xlsx. Trust the magic bytes, never the extension.
cases.notes: SheetError has no dedicated 'not an archive' case; archiveMalformed (zip.malformed) is it. The reader tells the two apart by the leading bytes: a file that starts with PK but has no end-of-central-directory record is truncated, one that never had a PK signature is malformed.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: An OLE2/CFB container advertising EncryptedPackage + EncryptionInfo - what Excel writes for a password-protected workbook. Must be distinguished from 'not a zip' so the UI can say 'password protected' instead of 'corrupt'.
cases.notes: Detect on the CFB magic D0CF11E0A1B11AE1, then look for EncryptedPackage. Workbook.meta.readOnlyReason must be set so A2 can never write it back.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: 12,004 entries. Every one costs an OpaqueParts slot, so the cap has to be enforced while READING the central directory, not after building the table.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.limit: Limits.maxEntryDecompressedBytes (200 MB), checked against the DECLARED size before allocating
cases.proves: A ~120-byte entry whose ZIP64 header declares 10 GB uncompressed. Reject on the declared size BEFORE allocating, then verify the actual inflated length matches.
cases.notes: Both halves matter: pre-allocating from a declared size is a DoS, and trusting the declared size after inflating hides a truncation. The declared-size check fires first here, which is why the code is zip.bomb.entry rather than a ratio error.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: The stored CRC32 is wrong. Silent bit-rot on a modelled part must be caught, because A2 will copy the bad bytes straight back out on the next save.
cases.notes: Verify the CRC of every entry you actually inflate. Entries passed through untouched keep their original CRC by construction.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: Method 99 = AES/WinZip encryption. Store (0) and deflate (8) are the only methods OOXML uses; anything else means the file is not what it claims.
cases.notes: Report the method number in the message - 99 means encrypted, 12/14 mean bzip2/LZMA, and the user-facing text should differ.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: <dimension> claims 4,294,967,296 rows and a row element sits at r=4294967295. Excel's ceiling is 1,048,576 x 16,384 (Limits).
cases.notes: Also proves the row index is parsed as Int64, not Int32 - 4294967295 overflows a signed 32-bit parse to -1. The dimension is checked before the row, so the dimension error is the one that fires.

cases.proves: 100,000 levels of element nesting. A recursive-descent parser blows the stack; a DOM parser allocates 100,000 nodes. A depth cap stops both.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: A 40,000-character cell. Excel's hard limit is 32,767 (see the accepted twin structure/long-cell-32k.xlsx at 32,763).
cases.notes: If A1 would rather truncate-and-flag than reject, that is defensible - but it must be a deliberate, tested, user-visible choice, not an accident.

mustNotHappen: truncating the string at the NUL and continuing silently
cases.proves: A raw NUL plus BEL and vertical tab inside <t>. All three are illegal in XML 1.0 and no conforming parser may accept them.
cases.notes: C1 carries the LEGAL escaped form _x0000_. A1 decodes _xHHHH_ escapes and drops any character XML 1.0 forbids rather than reintroducing it - and A2 must re-escape on write. SheetError.xmlInvalidEncoding is documented as covering 'a NUL inside a string', which is this.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: A structurally valid ZIP with [Content_Types].xml and rels but no xl/workbook.xml. The rels target dangles.
cases.notes: Resolve parts THROUGH the rels graph (A1's brief: never hardcode paths) and this surfaces as a named missing relationship target, not an index-out-of-range.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: Row 0 (rows are 1-based), an empty r="", a 5-letter column past XFD, a column with no row, a row with no column, and a negative row.
cases.notes: CellRef parsing is the most-called function in the codebase (A0's brief). It has to be both fast and total - every one of these must return nil, never trap.

mustNotHappen: reading any file outside the archive
cases.proves: Unclosed <c>, unclosed <worksheet>, mismatched nesting. The baseline 'garbage in' case.
cases.notes: The error must name the PART and ideally the byte offset. 'Could not open file' is not a diagnosis.
